title: My cost estimate for the new words was too low

blocks.label: Where this is
blocks.text: Release 1.0 › single tasks: the new words, parts 1 to 3 › before the build

blocks.label: What happened
blocks.text: I told you that the new words would cost 2 to 5 M tokens. The engineer's check, based on a past large task, gave 10 to 21 M tokens for the three pull requests: about four times more.

blocks.label: What I told you, and what is true

body.label: I said (11 Nov, before the design)
True
body.text: 10 to 21 M tokens and 13 to 26 h of agent time for all three pull requests (estimate, from the engineer's check).

body.label: If you acted on it
body.text: you approved the three pull requests at 18:43, after the check. Parts 2 and 3 have not started, so you can still change that answer.

blocks.label: What it changed for you
blocks.text: nothing to undo. The work costs more than I told you. Part 1 has used 1.0 M tokens so far.

blocks.label: What I did
blocks.text: recorded the corrected range and its basis in the logbook, and used it in the estimate for the three pull requests.

items: My first number had no basis in measured runs. The engineer's check used a past large task: 8.1 M tokens and 11 h.
The rule to give a basis is an instruction only. No check holds it.

blocks.label: Has it happened before
blocks.text: not that the logbook shows. The logbook does not keep my estimates, so a repeat would not show either.

items: Each estimate names its basis: measured runs of past tasks of the same size. prevent · todo (the estimate format)
I record each estimate that I give you, so the logbook can compare it with the measured cost. prevent · todo

blocks.label: What you need to do
blocks.text: nothing. If 10 to 21 M tokens is too much for the new words, tell me: parts 2 and 3 can wait.

blocks.label: Next update
blocks.text: none. This case is closed; the estimate format carries the fix.
